name: Tactical Fusion
description: Enriches conversations with mission-relevant context, including geospatial data, CoT, time zones, IP intelligence, CVEs, and other operational information.

settings_schema.header: Recognize mission-relevant context in messages and enrich it in place. [View the full documentation](/plugins/com.mattermost.plugin-tactical-fusion/public/help/help.html) for the formats, the sidebar panel, and troubleshooting.

sections.title: Date and time
sections.subtitle: The first switch governs this section. The formats below it are matched individually and all apply while it is on.

settings.help_text: Recognize times in messages and rewrite them as links that open a Date/Time panel.

Matches 091630ZAUG26, 091630ZAUG2026 and the short form 091630Z. Only applies while "Decorate date-time groups" is on. Turning a format off stops new messages being decorated with it; links already in existing messages keep working.

Matches 2026-08-09T16:30:00Z and 2026-08-09T20:30:00+04:00. Only applies while "Decorate date-time groups" is on. Turning a format off stops new messages being decorated with it; links already in existing messages keep working.

Matches a time introduced by the "DTG:" label, as some military formats write it, and drops the label from the link. Only labels the formats that are themselves on. Only applies while "Decorate date-time groups" is on. Turning a format off stops new messages being decorated with it; links already in existing messages keep working.

sections.title: Coordinates
sections.subtitle: The first switch governs this section. The formats below it are matched individually and all apply while it is on. Positions are always WGS 84; a coordinate carrying another datum is left alone rather than reinterpreted.

settings.help_text: Recognize geographic coordinates in messages and rewrite them as links that open a Location panel.

Matches 34.0561, -118.2500. Requires a comma and at least four decimal places on both values, which is what separates a coordinate from an ordinary pair of numbers; 34.05, -118.25 is deliberately left alone. This is the widest-reaching format, so turn this one off first if ordinary numbers in your channels are being linked. Only applies while "Decorate coordinates" is on.

settings.display_name: Format: latitude and longitude with hemisphere letters
settings.help_text: Matches 34.0561 N, 118.2500 W, 34°03'22"N 118°15'00"W and 34°03.366'N 118°15.000'W. Hemisphere letters are required, and a decimal point is required on the plain decimal form so that "Load 12 N, 5 W" is not read as a position. Only applies while "Decorate coordinates" is on.

Matches the fixed-width shapes used in ATO and USMTF traffic: 3510N07901W (LATM), 400948N1221400W (LATS), 331000.0N1183000.0W (LATDS and DMPID) and 3510N9-07901W7 (verified). The shortest shape, 35N079W (LATD), is only matched behind a field label. Only applies while "Decorate coordinates" is on.

Matches grid references written with spaces, such as 18S UJ 23478 06483, and run together in upper case at 100 m or finer, as 18SUJ2347806483. Lower case run together is not matched, because that is what a short git commit hash looks like, and neither is anything coarser, because a shorter run is what a part number looks like; both are still matched behind an MGRS: label. A grid reference is validated against the letter scheme of the zone it names, so a square that does not exist is left alone. Only applies while "Decorate coordinates" is on. A form that only ever matches behind its label, such as a lower-case or coarse run-together reference, also needs Format: labeled coordinate to be on.

settings.display_name: Format: UTM (off by default: the band letter is ambiguous)
settings.help_text: OFF BY DEFAULT, AND THE ONLY FORMAT THAT IS. A UTM token is ambiguous in a way no other coordinate here is. The letter after the zone number is read as a latitude band, following MGRS, so 11S 384640E 3769080N is band S and resolves to 34 north. Somebody using the civilian convention writes the same characters to mean "zone 11, southern hemisphere", which is 56 south: the same text, two readings, 90 degrees of latitude apart, and nothing in it says which was meant. The northing must land inside the band its letter names, which declines about nine in ten positions written the civilian way, but not all of them. Every other format here risks decorating something that was not a coordinate; this one risks decorating a real coordinate and pointing at the wrong place. Turn it on if your workspace writes UTM the military way, which is the common case for MGRS-speaking users. Matches 33U 291000 5628000 spaced, with optional axis letters as in 11S 384640E 3769080N; run together it is matched only behind a UTMO: or UTMT: label, since after the zone and band it is thirteen bare digits. Only applies while "Decorate coordinates" is on. A form that only ever matches behind its label, such as a lower-case or coarse run-together reference, also needs Format: labeled coordinate to be on.

Matches a World Geographic Reference System code such as GEOREF:GJPJ3718, and the finer GEOREF:GJPJ371183 and GEOREF:GJPJ37110183. GEOREF is written longitude first, and a code names a cell rather than a point, so the position shown for one is its center. This format is matched behind a GEOREF: label only, never bare: four letters and four digits has nothing in it a part number does not, so a bare pattern would rewrite ordinary text. It therefore also needs Format: labeled coordinate to be on. Only applies while "Decorate coordinates" is on.

Matches a Global Area Reference System code such as GARS:006AG, GARS:006AG3 and GARS:006AG39, which are cells of 30, 15 and 5 minutes. The position shown for one is the center of its cell. This format is matched behind a GARS: label only, never bare: seven alphanumerics whose only structural check is that just over a third of the letter pairs name no band is not enough to tell a coordinate from a part number. It therefore also needs Format: labeled coordinate to be on. Only applies while "Decorate coordinates" is on.

Matches a full Open Location Code such as 849VCWC8+R9, including the longer 849VCWC8+R9C and the padded, coarser 849V0000+. Unlike GEOREF and GARS this one is matched without a label, because its twenty-character alphabet contains no vowels and the separator sits at a fixed position, so an eight-character run of it is not a word. Unlabeled it is matched in upper case only, because a lower-case run of that shape is what a version string with build metadata looks like, and roughly one in 50,000 of those is a well-formed code; lower case is still matched behind a PLUSCODE: or OLC: label. Short codes such as CWC8+R9 are left alone: resolving one needs a nearby reference location this plugin does not have. A code names a cell, and the position shown for one is its center. Turn this off if your channels carry identifiers shaped like ABCDEFGH+IJ. Only applies while "Decorate coordinates" is on.

Matches a coordinate introduced by a field label such as LATM:, LATS:, DMPID:, GEOK:, MGRS:, UTMO: or UTMT:. The label is kept in the message rather than consumed, so a decorated line still reads as USMTF. Only labels the formats that are themselves on, and a label vouches for nothing: the coordinate behind it still has to be one. Only applies while "Decorate coordinates" is on.

sections.title: Maps
sections.subtitle: The first switch governs this section. The surfaces below it are drawn individually and all apply while it is on. Nothing here changes which coordinates are recognized.

settings.help_text: Draw a map showing where a decorated coordinate is. The basemap ships inside this plugin, so no tile service is called and nothing is fetched from outside your own server. Turning this off draws no map on any surface and stops clients requesting the basemap archive, its fonts and the map library, which together are the largest thing this plugin transfers. Only applies while "Decorate coordinates" is on.

settings.display_name: Map in the sidebar and hover card
settings.help_text: Draw the map beside a table of readings, wherever that table appears: the Location panel in the right-hand sidebar, the card shown when a reader points at a coordinate link, and the coordinate's own standalone page. That card is the map and nothing else, so turning this off removes the card rather than leaving an empty one. Readers can also hide the sidebar map for themselves under "Customize your view". Only applies while "Decorate coordinates" and "Draw maps for coordinates" are on.

Draw the map in the channel, under a post whose body this plugin renders: a message whose whole text is one coordinate, and a Cursor on Target event. This is the one setting here that changes the message itself: a post drawn this way is marked with a custom type, and Elasticsearch and OpenSearch index such a post but never match it, so it is missing from search and from Recent Mentions. Link previews, image embeds and automatic translation are dropped for it as well. Turning this off leaves those posts as ordinary messages and restores all of that. Installs searching through Postgres are unaffected either way. Only applies while "Decorate coordinates" and "Draw maps for coordinates" are on.

Serve the standalone page that gives the whole window to one map, which is what "Open larger" opens and what a client without the webapp bundle follows a coordinate link to. Turning this off makes that address answer "not found"; every reading is still available on the coordinate's own page. Only applies while "Decorate coordinates" and "Draw maps for coordinates" are on.

A directory on this server holding detail map packages, which are the OpenStreetMap archives drawn above zoom 10. Drop a file named <command>-<area>.pmtiles into it, such as indopacom-hawaii.pmtiles, and the area appears without restarting anything. A package here replaces a bundled one of the same name. Leave this empty to use only the packages the plugin ships. In a cluster every node must see this directory, because each node serves the archives it can read; a package on one node alone is drawn for some readers and not others.

Install or remove one detail map area. This writes into the package directory above, which is the same place a file copied there by hand is read from, because a map archive is served by byte range and has to sit on disk. Set the directory first. In a cluster an upload reaches only the node that served it.

sections.title: Airfields
sections.subtitle: Recognize ICAO airfield codes written behind a USMTF field label, and show the airfield and its position.

settings.help_text: Recognize an ICAO airfield code written behind ICAO:, LOC:, DEPLOC: or ARRLOC: and rewrite it as a link that opens an Airfield panel. A code is only recognized behind one of those labels, in upper case: four letters on their own are indistinguishable from ordinary words, and many airfield codes are ordinary words. Turning this off stops new messages being decorated; links already written keep working.

settings.display_name: Show the airfield details under a labeled code on its own
settings.help_text: When a message is nothing but one labeled airfield reference, such as "ICAO:KIND" or "DEPLOC:KIND//", add a table of the field's details under it: its name, where it is, what kind of field it is, its elevation and its IATA code. The table is written into the message itself, so it appears on every client, is included when messages are exported, and is what the author sees if they edit the post. The values are fixed when the message is posted and are not updated when a later plugin version corrects the database. Turning this off stops new messages being expanded; messages already posted keep their table. Only applies while "Decorate airfield codes" is on.

sections.title: Cursor on Target
sections.subtitle: Render a Cursor on Target event pasted into a message or attached to a post, with its position on a map.

settings.help_text: Recognize a Cursor on Target event written in a fenced code block labeled cot or xml, and render it as a card with the event's identity, position, timing and accuracy. A post rendered this way is marked with a custom type, and Elasticsearch and OpenSearch index such a post but never match it, so it is missing from search and from Recent Mentions. Link previews, image embeds, file attachment lists and automatic translation are dropped for it as well, and any text written around the event renders without Markdown formatting. Turning this off leaves new posts as ordinary messages and restores all of that; posts already rendered keep their card. Installs searching through Postgres are unaffected either way.

settings.display_name: Read a Cursor on Target file attached to a post
settings.help_text: When a post carries exactly one attachment named .cot or .xml, read it and render the event it contains. This is the only setting in this plugin that reads a file while a message is being posted, so an install whose file storage is slow or remote may prefer to turn it off and keep the fenced code block, which costs nothing extra. Files over 64 KB are ignored either way. Only applies while "Render Cursor on Target events" is on.
